_meta.description: Irrigation decomposition. Agreste publishes a single departmental yield per crop that MIXES irrigated and rain-fed area. Applying that mixed mean to a rain-fed parcel overstates its yield, and the error is largest exactly where it matters: soybean, whose French area is majority irrigated. Without this correction the engine recommends rain-fed soy in Beauce, which almost no farmer actually grows there.
_meta.method: observed_mean = s * y_rainfed * (1 + uplift) + (1 - s) * y_rainfed, so y_rainfed = observed_mean / (1 + s * uplift), where s is the irrigated share of that crop's national area.
_meta.source: Irrigated shares and irrigation yield responses consistent with Agreste irrigation surveys and Terres Inovia / Terres Univia irrigation trial references.
_meta.caution: Shares are national averages applied uniformly. A department-by-crop irrigation share would be better and exists in the Agreste irrigation survey, which is not in the bulk series-longues file.

soybean.note: French soy is majority irrigated. Rain-fed soy north of the Loire is genuinely marginal and the engine should say so.

chickpea.note: Chickpea is grown precisely because it does not need water; irrigation adds little.

field_pea.note: Irrigation at flowering protects pod set in a dry June.

fava_bean.note: Fava bean is shallow rooted and responds strongly to water at flowering.

green_lentil.note: Lentil is almost never irrigated and over-watering causes lodging and staining.
